territorial_scope.description: Binding and directly applicable in all EU Member States; Article 44 also sets conditions for mutual recognition agreements with third countries that wish to have their certification recognised in the Union.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

summary.short: Implementing Regulation laying down the EUCC, the European Common Criteria-based cybersecurity certification scheme for ICT products and protection profiles under Regulation (EU) 2019/881. It sets assurance levels, evaluation and certification rules, monitoring, vulnerability handling and conformity-body requirements, applying from 27 February 2025.
summary.long: The Regulation sets out the European Common Criteria-based cybersecurity certification scheme (EUCC) for ICT products and protection profiles under Regulation (EU) 2019/881. Certificates are issued at assurance level 'substantial' (AVA_VAN 1 or 2) or 'high' (AVA_VAN 3, 4 or 5), evaluated under the Common Criteria and Common Evaluation Methodology (Arts 3-4). Self-assessment is not permitted (Art 6). AVA_VAN 4 or 5 certification is possible only in specified scenarios (Art 7(3)). Certificate validity generally does not exceed 5 years, with derogation subject to prior national approval (Art 12). Certification bodies operating at 'high' and ITSEF require national authorisation (Arts 21-22). Certificate holders must monitor vulnerabilities and perform vulnerability impact analyses (Arts 33-35). Certificates may be suspended for up to 42 days or withdrawn (Arts 14, 30). National authorities sample at least 4% of certificates annually (Art 25(3)), and certification bodies issuing 'high' certificates undergo peer assessment at least every five years (Art 45). Holders may affix a mark and label (Art 11). Third countries may seek mutual recognition agreements (Art 44). National certification schemes cease to produce effects 12 months after entry into force (Art 49). The Regulation applies from 27 February 2025 (Art 50).

relations.note: Enabling act: the Regulation is adopted under Article 49(7) of Regulation (EU) 2019/881. The EUCC scheme is set out in accordance with the certification framework of that Regulation (Recital 1, Article 1).

notes: Target instrument IDs are not given because the targets are not identified in the registry metadata; target_text names them instead. Text points to check: Recital 16 says a protection profile certificate covers 5 years as a minimum, while Article 18(2) says validity may be up to the lifetime of the protection profile. Annex I contains the placeholder '[date of entry into force]', Annex II point 2 reads '[BLANK]', and the Annex IX mark and label drawing is not reproduced in the text. Article 28(2) contains the wording 'other relevant Union legislation regulation'. Article 49(1) provides that national certification schemes covered by the EUCC cease to produce effects 12 months after entry into force; these national schemes are not registry instruments and no relation row is recorded for them.
